entities.summary: Latvia, officially the Republic of Latvia, is a country in the Baltic region of northern Europe. It is one of the three Baltic states, along with Estonia to the north and Lithuania to the south. It borders Russia to the east and Belarus to the southeast and shares a maritime border with Sweden to the west. Latvia covers an area of 64,573 km2 (24,932 sq mi), with a population of 1.83 million. The country has a temperate seasonal climate. Its capital and largest city is Riga. Latvians, who are the titular nation and comprise 65.5% of the country's population, belong to the ethnolinguistic group of the Balts and speak Latvian.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Latvia played a significant role in World War II, with over 200,000 Latvians serving in the German Wehrmacht and approximately 50,000 Latvian Jews being deported to concentration camps. The country's resistance movement, led by the Daugavpils garrison, contributed to the Soviet Union's capture of Riga in 1944.
